subject: Draft MAP: exit gates, acceptance probes, and test owners
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@carelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP: exit gates, acceptance probes, and test owners

Laura — attaching the first-cut MAP and a compact acceptance-tests CSV. High level: I captured the success criteria we discussed on the call plus three hard exit gates we think should be non-negotiable for production. Quick summary below and next steps at the bottom.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Success criteria: 95% intent-routing accuracy on our 10k sample, sub-200ms 95th perc. on P95 path, and no PII leakage above baseline in redaction spot checks.
- Exit gates: performance (SLO hit for 7 consecutive days), safety (no high-severity false-positive leak), and operational (autoscaler and KV cache verified under synthetic load).
- Acceptance probes: 8 automated smoke scenarios, 4 stress experiments, and 6 labelled edge-case checks — owners and test data in the attached CSV.

Please review the exit gates and the proposed owners column in the CSV — Ben and Marissa are looped to confirm operational runbooks and test scheduling. If you’re good with this scope, we’ll lock the MAP and schedule the verification runway (week-of Apr 19) with daily check-ins.

Attachments: 20270401-MAP-v1.docx (MAP narrative + timeline), acceptance-tests.csv (test matrix and owners)

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@carelytics.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@carelytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: exit gates, acceptance probes, and test owners

Thanks, Olga. This is very helpful — I skimmed the doc and CSV. Two quick clarifications before we lock it:

1) For the P95 latency gate, can we define the measurement path as our typical HL7 ingestion -> inference -> normalized output? I want that explicit so we don’t end up measuring a trimmed path.
2) For the safety probe, the CSV has a "PII redaction spot checks" entry — can you confirm sample size and that we’ll run those against our in-house PHI-synth set, not live data?

Samir (copied) will own the in-house smoke execution. He — if you can confirm the dataset availability and a preferred window for the stress run, we’ll align with Redwood’s ops availability.

—Laura
Director of Product, Carelytics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: exit gates, acceptance probes, and test owners

Adding operational detail per Laura's ask. Olga — I updated the CSV (column: measurement-path) and added precise checklist steps for the P95 path. Highlights:

- Measurement path: HL7 -> preproc -> full inference runtime (including tokenization and KV cache hit/miss) -> postproc. We will capture token-level timestamps to isolate model vs. infra cost.
- PII redaction spot checks: we'll use your PHI-synth set (Samir confirm) and run 500 randomized records per run, 3 runs per day during verification window.
- Stress plan: synthetic load generator + long-tail scenario runner; target: 2x expected peak for 2 hours, then a 6-hour soak at 1.5x with telemetry collection.

I attached a short operational checklist to the Drive link (see related_links). Marissa — can you confirm runbook owners and whether we should schedule a joint dry run on Apr 12?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Apr 19-23: verification window (daily 9:00 standup, telemetry review at 17:00).
- Apr 26: cutover decision meeting (review pass/fail across all probes).

I’ll create a calendar invite once Samir confirms dataset availability and preferred dry-run times. Also, I’ll add a row in the CSV indicating who is responsible for incident escalation (tier-2 ops: Ben; tier-3: Olga).
